svg.title: Biologically relevant differences between DNA and RNA
svg.desc: Comparison table: cellular DNA is usually double-stranded, contains 2-prime-deoxyribose and uses A, T, G, C bases; RNA is usually single-stranded but can fold into paired regions, contains ribose with a 2-prime hydroxyl and uses A, U, G, C. RNA examples include messenger, transfer and ribosomal RNA.

g.text: DNA and RNA: compare the properties the IB requires
A1.2.7 · complement the adjacent ribose/deoxyribose structural sketch
Usually one strand; may fold and pair
Both are nucleotide polymers with covalent sugar–phosphate backbones; 2′ describes the carbon position on the pentose sugar.
